title: Derived compact-support retraction from a prime-to-primary finite etale cover
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and use $D^+(S_{\Et},\Lambda)$ for bounded-below derived categories of module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $T,X,Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, $h:X\to Y$ separated of finite type and $g:T\to X$ finite etale [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Choose compactifications $c_h,c_{hg}$, where a compactification is $c=(j,p)$ with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper, and set $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$, let $\ell$ be prime and $n\geq1$, and assume $\ell^nF=0$. Suppose every geometric fibre of $g$ has the same cardinality $d\geq1$, with $\ell\nmid d$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre]. Write $g^{-1},g_*$ and $\eta:F\to g_*g^{-1}F$ for inverse image, direct image and their adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and $G[0]$ for a sheaf placed in degree zero. There is an isomorphism in $D^+(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$
$$\alpha:Rh_!^{c_h}((g_*g^{-1}F)[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R(hg)_!^{c_{hg}}((g^{-1}F)[0]).$$
There are morphisms $u:Rh_!^{c_h}(F[0])\to R(hg)_!^{c_{hg}}((g^{-1}F)[0])$ and $v$ in the reverse direction with $v\circ u=1$, and $u=\alpha\circ Rh_!^{c_h}(\eta[0])$. No invertibility of $d$ in $\Lambda$, local constancy of $F$, or connectedness of $X,T$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GKY, label lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1, trace-splitting and shriek-composition paragraph. Derived formulation of the argument, using finite direct-image exactness and the identity compactification of a finite morphism.

proof.text: Put E = g^*F and take the counit t of the proved finite-etale reverse adjunction g_* ⊣ g^*. Private unit_stalk_component identifies the ordinary unit on each algebraically closed stalk with the diagonal, using naturality of upperStarCompSheafFiberIso and the ordinary adjunction triangle. Private trace_stalk_component identifies t on each summand with the pullback stalk comparison, using finiteEtaleUnit_stalk_inclusion and the reverse adjunction triangle. The finite stalk product has identity equal to the sum of projection-inclusion composites, by sheafFiberToLowerStar_stalkRestrict and its off-diagonal zero formula. Thus eta followed by t has stalk equal to a sum of Nat.card(g.GeometricFiber s) identities. Apply the given algebraically closed degree hypothesis and conservativity of algebraically closed geometric stalks. This proves private exists_trace_algClosed directly from the given hypothesis, avoiding the separably closed formulation of the existing trace-degree API.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), Definition 03SE (definition-trace-map) and the following degree formula

proof.text: The prime hypothesis gives Nat.Coprime d (ell^n). Private generic primary_unit_split applies Nat.gcd_eq_gcd_ab to obtain a*d + b*ell^n = 1, with a = Nat.gcdA d (ell^n). Distribute integer scalar multiplication on morphisms and use ell^n • id_F = 0. Then rho = a • t satisfies eta followed by rho = id_F. This uses the additive morphism group, not invertibility in Lambda.

proof.text: Apply the existing proved instance preservesFiniteColimits_lowerStar_of_isFinite directly with ModuleCat Lambda. It already applies to these concrete coefficients, so no auxiliary forgetful-functor argument is needed. Together with the usual finite-limit preservation it supplies exactness of g_*.

source.place: Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero); coefficient lift using sites-modules.tex Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian)

proof.text: Finite g is proper. Construct cg = (id_T,g). The source isomorphism upperStarIsoOpenImmersionLowerShriekInv at Iso.refl T followed by upperStarId identifies (id_T)_! with the identity. Apply mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryPlusIdIso, then whisker by R+g_* to identify Rg_!^cg with R+g_*. The proved specialized rightDerivedFunctorPlusIsoMapDerivedCategoryPlus for the exact g_*, together with mapDerivedCategoryPlusSingleFunctor at degree zero, gives beta: (g_*E)[0] ≅ Rg_!^cg(E[0]). The specialized canonical exact-derived API avoids constructing a general Kan-extension factorization witness.

source.place: Tag 0GKY (lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1), finite-cover composition argument; identity compactification and derived.tex Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-qcqs-composition] to $T\xrightarrow{g}X\xrightarrow{h}Y$ and to $c_g,c_h,c_{hg}$. The schemes are qcqs, both maps are separated of finite type, and the coefficient ring is finite, exactly as required. Evaluating its natural isomorphism at $E[0]$ gives $C_E:Rh_!^{c_h}Rg_!^{c_g}(E[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R(hg)_!^{c_{hg}}(E[0])$. Define $\alpha=C_E\circ Rh_!^{c_h}(\beta)$. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so this is the asserted isomorphism from $Rh_!^{c_h}(H[0])$. The cited composition statement permits the originally specified compactifications independently; no compatible choice or extra compactification-independence assertion is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), applied to the finite cover; Tag 0GKY, displayed equality Rf_! g_* g^{-1}F = R(fg)_! g^{-1}F

proof.text: Write $A=Rh_!^{c_h}$, $K=F[0]$ and $L=H[0]$. Passing the sheaf maps of step 2 to complexes concentrated in degree zero and then localizing preserves their composite, so $\rho[0]\circ\eta[0]=\operatorname{id}_K$. Define $u=\alpha\circ A(\eta[0])$ and $v=A(\rho[0])\circ\alpha^{-1}$. Then $v\circ u=A(\rho[0])\circ\alpha^{-1}\circ\alpha\circ A(\eta[0])=A(\rho[0]\circ\eta[0])=A(\operatorname{id}_K)=\operatorname{id}_{A(K)}$. These formulas give both the retraction and exactly the required formula for $u$.

I read the item and every cited statement in full. Sources checked: Stacks 0GKY (lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1: trace splitting F→g_*g^{-1}F→F and Rf_!g_*g^{-1}F = R(fg)_!g^{-1}F), 03SH (trace method) and 0F7J (shriek composition for separated finite-type morphisms of qcqs schemes). Step 1: the coefficient-linear trace node gives t∘η = d·id with arbitrary R and no connectedness. Advisory: that node counts lifts of separably closed points while def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre uses algebraically closed ones. For finite étale g the counts agree (a finite étale scheme over a separably closed field is a disjoint union of copies of the point), the node itself calls its count 'the geometric fibre', and split-locally-constant-retraction reads it the same way. Step 2: Bezout ad+bℓ^n=1 and ℓ^n·id_F=0 give ρη=id; correct. Step 3: forget is faithful and exact and commutes with module g_*, so it reflects exactness of finite g_*. The two curve-estimates generic tools are declared in tool_uses, and the chapter uses sec-curve-estimates. Step 4: finite⇒proper, the identity compactification is explicit in its definition, (1_T)_!≅id from the presheaf definition, and the exact-functor node gives (g_*E)[0]≅Rg_*(E[0]). Step 5: the qcqs-composition hypotheses (finite Λ, qcqs schemes, separated finite type, three arbitrary compactifications) all hold, and α=C_E∘Rh_!(β) has the right direction. Step 6: v∘u=id with the required formula for u. Edge cases: Λ=Z/6 with ℓ=2 and d=3 (d not a unit in Λ) works; ℓ|d fails as expected; X=∅ is trivial. No cycle: the closure of qcqs-composition does not contain the item. Not on the drop list. Route: trace-degree is sk-thm-p1, forgetful is sk-thm-reduction, exact-functor is sk-def-exchange, qcqs-composition is the item's own unit; no SGA. Batch-5 flag (qcqs-composition → lem-pod-lisse-module-sheaves-as-module-objects): accepted. The item's only citer, lisse-open-relative-line-constructibility, already reaches both nodes without the item, so the closure is unchanged. The pod node (lisse = module objects in FLC) is generic and is not a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality proofs, and 0F7J composition is a general six-functor tool. No fixes.
